name: Settings switches
summary: A group of on and off settings, each with a plain explanation, including one that is locked by the organization.
use: on a settings page with on and off options
a11y: Native checkboxes with role switch inside their labels, so the whole row is the target; the switch is at least 24 px tall; a setting the organization locked shows its state in words with a lock and is read as "On, locked".

use_when: admin or security settings where some options are set by the organization and the person must see that they cannot change them
avoid_when: a setting with more than two choices: use a select or radio group, as member-list does for roles
choosing a paid plan: use plan-picker
quick on and off controls for devices: use home-controls

parts.name: settings
parts.what: one setting: name, explanation and its switch or lock; the whole row is the target

parts.name: help
parts.what: a plain explanation of the effect

parts.name: switch
parts.what: a native checkbox shown as a switch

parts.name: locked
parts.what: a locked setting's state in words with a lock, in place of the switch

empty.how: with no settings in the group, leave the group out rather than showing an empty box

loading.how: keep the rows and set disabled on each switch until its saved value arrives

error.how: if a change fails to save, flip the switch back and show the reason in toast-stack

disabled.how: a setting the organization locked shows its state in words with a lock, read as 'On, locked'; a disabled switch is also styled faded

overflow.how: the group grows with every row; past about eight, split it into several groups with their own titles

long_text.how: names and explanations wrap beside the switch, the title breaks anywhere to fit, and the locked state never wraps

keyboard: Tab reaches each switch in turn; locked settings have no control and are skipped
Space turns the focused switch on or off
